card: Adds test vectors verifying P2SH script evaluation behavior at the 1,000-item stack size limit boundary. Existing script test vectors do not test this boundary, allowing alternative node implementations that verify the redeemScript hash without executing the scriptPubKey to pass all test cases while accepting invalid 1,000-item spends. The PR adds 999- and 1,000-item test rows to script tests and a spender to the functional tests for export to qa-assets.
evidence: PR description: 'An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row.'
PR description: 'These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (rbitcoin)'
problem: Existing test vectors omit coverage for scriptSigs that push the stack right up to the 1,000-item limit before the P2SH scriptPubKey runs. As a result, non-compliant Bitcoin implementations that bypass executing the scriptPubKey and merely compare redeemScript hashes can pass all existing test vectors despite violating consensus rules on 1,000-item spends.

risk.why: Test-only changes that cannot affect consensus validation or node behavior in production.

summary: Adds script and functional test cases covering the 1,000-element stack size limit boundary during P2SH execution. It verifies that when a scriptSig leaves 1,000 items on the stack, the 20-byte hash push during scriptPubKey evaluation triggers a stack size limit failure, whereas 999 items succeeds. It also adds a corresponding spender case to the feature_taproot functional test for export to the QA script test assets.
uncertainties: The patch diff was not provided, although the PR description and commit messages detail the exact test cases added.
